answer_text: Inflation refers to a general and sustained increase in the overall price level of goods and services across an economy over time, which means that, on average, the same amount of money buys progressively less than it used to. This erosion of money's purchasing power is the key practical consequence of inflation: if your income doesn't rise at least as fast as prices are rising, your real standard of living effectively falls even though the number on your paycheck stays the same or grows more slowly.
